questions.question: What is the outermost layer found in the cell envelope of the bacterial cell called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glycocalyx**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Glycocalyx:

 
 
• It is a **surface layer that covers the cell membrane of many bacteria, epithelial cells or other cells.**
 
• It is made up of** proteoglycans, glycoproteins and glycolipids.**
 
• Glycocalyx is a** viscous polysaccharide or polypeptide slime that covers microbes.**
 
• It enhances adherence to surfaces. resists phagocytic engulfment by the white blood cells.
 
• It prevents antibiotics from contacting the microbe.
 
 
 
• Functions:
 
 
• ​It protects the cell from dehydration **(capsule).**
 
• It protects the bacterial cell from engulfment and destruction by the immune system's white blood cells (capsule).
 
• Glycocalyx gives the bacterial cell a sticky character which enables it to attach to surfaces.
 
• Glycocalyx also helps the bacterial cells to adhere to each other. This forms a bacterial aggregate that can't be engulfed by the immune cells.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The bacterial cell wall is made up of peptidoglycans (also known as murein), diaminopimelic acid, and teichoic acid.
 
• All three molecules are unique to prokaryotes and not found in eukaryotes.

questions.question: President Droupadi Murmu has appointed Dr. Justice Dhananjaya Yashwant Chandrachud as the _______ Chief Justice of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50th**__.

• Justice DY Chandrachud to Take Oath As New Chief Justice of IndiaSenior-most Supreme Court judge and Chief Justice of India-designate Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud is all set to become the 50th head of the Indian judiciary when President Draupadi Murmu would administer the oath of office to him at Rashtrapati Bhawan.
 
• Justice Chandrachud, born on November 11, 1959, was elevated to the top court on May 13, 2016.
 
• He has been part of several Constitution benches and landmark verdicts of the top court including on matters relating to the Ayodhya land dispute, the right to privacy and adultery.

questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution of India reflects the Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Part IV-A__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties are defined as the moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• These duties set out in Part IV–A of the Constitution, concern individuals and the nation.
 
• The 11 fundamental duties are -
 
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect the national flag & National Anthem
 
• Follow the ideals of the freedom struggle
 
• Protect the sovereignty & integrity of India
 
• Defend the country and render national services when called upon
 
• Spirit of common brotherhood
 
• Preserve composite culture
 
• Preserve natural environment
 
• Develop scientific temper
 
• Safeguard public property
 
• Strive for excellence
 
• Duty for all parents/guardians to send their children in the age group of 6-14 years to school.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Part X of the Indian Constitution entails the provisions related to Scheduled and Tribal Areas with Articles 244 – 244 A.
 
• Part XII of the Indian constitution deals with finance, property, contracts and suits. It covers articles 264-300A.
 
• **Part IX-B**
 
 
• ​The Constitution (97th Amendment) Act, 2011 inserted Part IX-B in the Indian constitution.
 
• It deals with Co-operative Societies.

questions.question: How many maximum electrons can M shell have?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Concept:__

 __
 
• The distribution of electrons into different orbits of an atom was suggested by Bohr and Bury.
 
• The orbits or shells are represented by the letters K, L, M, N,… or the numbers, n = 1, 2, 3, 4.
 
• The following rules are followed for writing the number of electrons in different energy levels or shells:
 
• The maximum number of electrons present in a shell is given by the formula 2n2, where ‘n’ is the orbit number or energy level index. 
 
 
 
• Calculation:__
 __
 
• Given:__
 
• Shell given = M, orbit number = 3.
 
• The maximum number of electrons present in a shell is given by the formula 2n2.
 
• **Therefore, 2 × 32 = 18**

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct?

I. The nutrition requirements of adolescents are higher than adults.

II. Adolescents are generally grouped in the age group of 10 to 19 years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adolescents need more nutrients than adults **because they gain at least 40 per cent of their adult weight and 15 per cent of their adult height during this period.
 
• Inadequate intake can lead to delayed sexual development and slower linear growth.
 
 
• **Hence Statement 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• Adolescents are generally grouped in the age group** of 10 to 19 years. **
 
 
• **Hence Statement 2 is correct.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Adolescence **is characterized by rapid physical, social, mental, and emotional changes.
 
• It is also a time of opportunity and risk. In the view of Stanley Hall (the father of adolescent psychology), it’s a time of “storm and stress.”
 
 
• Adolescence is a period of rapid growth when young people acquire new abilities and face new challenges, in this stage children are in conflict with their parents, are moody, and tend to spend more time with their peers.
 
• It is the transitional stage of childhood and adulthood when a child develops physically and psychologically into an adult.
 
• Adolescents fail to think clearly, creating great frustration and stress in their lives.
 
• It is also known as the problem age because rapid physical growth leaves teenagers feeling awkward, self-conscious, uncoordinated, embarrassed, and even confused.

• **A poor conductor** call a component of identical size that offers higher resistance to electricity
 
• A material with high resistivity which means it has got high resistance and will resist the flow of electrons is called** insulating material.**

questions.question: Which of the following is celebrated as the "Tibetan New Year"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Losar festival.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Losar festival **marks the beginning of the **Tibetan New Year.**
 
• The Losar Festival is celebrated with **great zeal and fervour in Tibetian border states like Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It is also known as a festival of happiness and prosperity.
 
• The celebrates the** Ladakhi or Tibetan New Year. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Puthandu:

 
 
• It is also known as Puthuvarusham.
 
• Puthandu is observed by Tamils as the traditional "Tamil/Hindu New Year."
 
• It normally occurs on April 14 and this month is known as Chittirai, the first month of the Tamil solar calendar.
 
 
 
• Poila Boisakh:
 
 
• The first day of the first month of Baishakh in the Bengali solar calendar is known as Pohela Boishakh.
 
• It is also known as the Bengali New Year or Nobo Borso.
 
• It is widely observed in Bangladesh and West Bengal.
 
 
 
• Vishu:
 
 
• Due to Malyalam being the dominant language in Kerala, Vishu is sometimes referred to as the Malyalam New Year.
 
• For residents of Kerala and several nearby regions of Tamil Nadu, Vishu signifies the start of the new year.
 
 
 
• Gudi Padwa:
 
 
• Celebrated on the first day of Chaitra month, Gudi Padwa is a New Year day for Maharashtrians and Konkanis.
 
• On this day a gudi can be found hanging out on the right side of the main access of the houses.
 
 
 
• Navreh
 
 
• It is the lunar new year that is celebrated in Kashmir.
 
• It is the Sanskrit word ‘Nav-Varsha’ from where the word ‘Navreh’ has been derived.
 
• It falls on the first day of the Chaitra Navratri.
 
 
 
• Ugadi
 
 
• The festival of Ugadi is celebrated on the first day of Chaitra month as per the Hindu calendar
 
• Ugadi, also known as Yugadi, is a renowned South Indian festival mainly celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Telangana to commemorate the beginning of a new year.
 
• For Ugadi, doors in homes are adorned with mango leaf decorations called toranalu or Torana in Kannada
 
 
 
• Pana Sankranti
 
 
• Oriya New Year is also known as Pana Sankranti and it is observed as the first day of the Oriya Calendar.
 
• It is also known as ‘Maha Vishuba Sankranti,’ ‘Maha Sankranti,’ and ‘Mesha Sankranti’ is a festival that is widely celebrated across Odisha as the traditional New Year
 
• Pana Sankranti is named after ‘Pana,’ the main fruit drink which is prepared in Odisha’s traditional culture.

questions.question: Which layer of atmosphere helps in radio transmission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thermosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The thermosphere layer of the Atmosphere helps in Radio Transmission.
 
• It is located above the mesosphere and below the exosphere.
 
• In the thermosphere, the temperature rises rapidly with increasing height.
 
• The ionosphere is a part of this layer. 
 
• This layer helps in radio transmission and in fact, radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• This layer is home to the International Space Station as it orbits Earth. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The troposphere

 
• It is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• Its average height is 13 km and extends roughly to a height of 8 km near the poles and about 18 km at the equator.
 
• The thickness of the troposphere is greatest at the equator because heat is transported to great heights by strong convectional currents.
 
• This layer contains dust particles and water vapor.
 
• All changes in climate and weather take place in this layer.
 
• The temperature in this layer decreases at the rate of 1°C for every 165m of height.
 
• This is the most important layer for all biological activity.

The stratosphere

 
• It is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains the ozone layer.
 
• This layer absorbs ultraviolet radiation and shields life on the earth from an intense, harmful form of energy.

The mesosphere

 
• It lies above the stratosphere, which extends up to a height of 80 km.
 
• In this layer, once again, the temperature starts decreasing with the increase in altitude and reaches up to minus 100°C at a height of 80 km.
 
• The upper limit of the mesosphere is known as mesopause.

The exosphere

 
• It is the uppermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• This is the highest layer but very little is known about it.
 
• Whatever contents are there, these are extremely rarefied in this layer, and it gradually merges with outer space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21113c353f20b414120b928052c6703b99c375a2d5c054984abd57ad07f68029.png]

__
 
• All players are allowed unlimited let serves in table tennis.
 
• There is **no limit to let serves in table tennis.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Important terms of Table tennis:**

 
 
• Rally- Rally is a term used in Tennis. The period in which the ball is in play.
 
• Let- Service ball hitting the net or a distraction that causes the point played over.
 
• Point- A unit of scoring in table tennis.
 
• Dead - A ball without any spin.

questions.question: The value of GDP at the current prevailing prices is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nominal GDP**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The gross domestic product (GDP) **value at the most recent prices is known as **nominal GDP**.
 
• It is determined by current market pricing, without taking into account the** impact of inflation or deflation**.
 
• It shows how much money was spent on the commodities and services a nation generated within a certain fiscal year. In contrast to real GDP, which measures the rate of price rises in an economy, nominal GDP excludes changes in prices brought on by inflation.
 
• Due to the fact that real GDP only takes into account production and is unaffected by changes in prices or exchange rates, it is regarded as a reliable measure of a nation's economic progress.
 
• Growing pricing rather than an increase in the number of goods and services produced may be the cause of nominal GDP growth from year to year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real gross domestic product (GDP)**, which refers to the volume level of GDP, is GDP expressed at constant prices.
 
• By quantifying the values of all the goods and services produced in a given year in terms of a base period, one can derive constant price estimates of GDP.
 
• The standard measurement of the value added produced via the production of goods and services in a nation over a specific time period is the **gross domestic product (GDP)**.
 
• Consequently, it also accounts for the revenue generated by that manufacturing, or the total amount spent on finished goods and services (fewer imports).

questions.question: During which of the following period Ostriches were found in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Palaeolithic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **During Palaeolithic period, Ostriches** were found in **India**.
 
• At **Patne in Maharashtra**, significant numbers of ostrich eggshells were discovered.
 
• Indian researchers have for the first time discovered molecular proof to support the presence of these birds in India more than 25,000 years ago based on a DNA examination of an ostrich fossilized eggshell fragment. Scientists from the CCMB, Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee, and other institutions collaborated to conduct the study.
 
• The continental drift of Gondwanaland or Gondwana is frequently cited as the cause of the ostrich's origin and evolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Paleolithic**, also known as the Old Stone Age, was a time in prehistoric human history marked by the invention of stone implements. It encompasses nearly the entire span of prehistoric human technology.
 
• A term used in archaeology to refer to particular cultures that existed between the Paleolithic and Neolithic periods is the **Mesolithic Period**, also known as the Middle Stone Age.
 
• Between the Neolithic and the Bronze Age lies a period known as the **Chalcolithic**, or Copper Age. It is believed to have started in the late fourth to early third millennia BC, depending on the location, and ended with the start of the Bronze Age proper.
 
• The third and last phase of the Stone Age was known as the **Neolithic Age**, or New Stone Age.

questions.question: The Maharashtra Department of Prisons has launched a loan scheme for inmates serving sentences in jails across the state. This credit scheme is titled _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jivhala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Maharashtra Department of Prisons **has introduced a financing programme called **Jivhala** for prisoners serving terms in various institutions throughout** Maharashtra**.

 This recently introduced credit programme, called Jivhala, is provided by **Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank**.
 
• For Indian convicts, a first-of-its-kind credit programme has been introduced. The current loan programmes that the banks are offering to the nation's prisoners are only intended to be used for rehabilitation when their prison terms are complete. 
 
• **The Yerawada Central Jail** inmates in Pune are the subjects of the pilot programme for this programme. About sixty prisons in Maharashtra will use this programme.
 
• This programme was primarily created for all convicted criminals serving sentences of more than three years.
 
• 230 loan applications from the Yerawada Central Prison are being processed during the scheme's pilot phase.
 
• There have been 222 male and 8 female loan applications out of the total.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Loans over Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh would be offered under the** "Kishor" Scheme**.
 
• A savings programme supported by the Indian government and geared towards parents of girls is known as **Sukanya Samriddhi Account**. The programme encourages parents to start a fund for their female child's future education.
 
• A government of India incentive for the unorganised sector is the **Swavalamban Scheme**. The Government of India will pay Rs. 1000 annually to each NPS-Swavalamban account as long as the contribution is between Rs. 1000 and Rs. 12000 annually. This pension programme is intended to provide retirement benefits to the unorganised sector.

questions.question: In which state is the Maihar court where Baba Allauddin Khan was a musician?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh **is the **Maihar court** where **Baba Allauddin Khan** was a musician.
 
• Baba Allauddin Khan was a musician for the Maihar court and was awarded **the Padma Bhushan in 1958 and the Padma Vibhushan in 1971.**
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar and Nikhil Banerjee,** both deceased, were two more notable artists from this Gharana.
 
• The nal-tarang, jal-tarang, and Chandra-Sarang, among other musical instruments, were created by Baba Allauddin Khan despite the restricted resources in a tiny town like Maihar.
 
• Baba founded the Maihar Band in 1918 with the intention of offering comfort to children who had been left orphaned by an epidemic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Baba Allauddin Khan was appointed as the **Maharaja of Maihar's court musician. **
 
• By creating a number of ragas, fusing the bass sitar and bass sarod with more conventional instruments, and assembling an orchestra, he created the groundwork for the present Maihar Gharana.
 
• He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi's highest honor, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, for his lifelong contribution to Indian music in 1954.
 
• He also received India's third and second-highest civilian honors, the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan, in 1958 and 1971, respectively.

questions.question: Which company has set up a factory on the banks of river Hugli in 1651?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**English**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **English** set up a factory on t**he banks of river Hugli **in **1651**.
 
• In 1651, Hugli became the site of the** first British factory**.
 
• The East India Company obtained a charter from **Queen Elizabeth I of England in 1600**, giving it the exclusive right to trade with the East and shielding it from other British traders' competition.
 
• Employees of the Company were obliged to pay duty because they also engaged in their own private businesses.
 
• However, they refused, infuriating Murshid Quli Khan, the Nawab of Bengal, which sparked a series of bloody wars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Hugli Riverfront** is made up of the two banks of the river, which flows through **West Bengal**, India, between the cities of Kolkata on the **east and Howrah on the west**.
 
• A beautifying project on the river's east bank began in 2011, and the first phase was completed in 2012. 
 
• The Ganga, also known as the Kati-Ganga in the Puranas, is a branch of the Bhagirathi Hooghly River that originates in Murshidabad, close to Giria, north of Baharampur and Palashi.
 
• The Padma, the major branch of the Ganges, then empties into Bangladesh.
